answer: Sybil resistance combines EigenTrust-style eigenvector centrality with exponential reputation decay: each score has a fixed temporal half-life, so credibility requires sustained honest service rather than a brief burst of activity. Reciprocity-weighted transitivity anchors trust in established peers, limiting fabricated endorsements. Freshly spawned sybil identities begin with near-zero centrality and cannot pass consensus; like a vine entering a river, they must earn trust through time, not spiral upward on self-created links.
